chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Rabbah ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): They narrate that Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, a completion of your Hajj is your Ihram from the Duwairah of your people.' He said, 'Glory be to Allah. If it were as they say, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have enjoyed his garments until the Tree. Rather, the meaning of the Duwairah of his people is those whose people were behind the Miqat towards Mecca.'
And the resident of Mecca goes out to the Miqat of his people for Hajj and Umrah together. If he is unable to do that, he enters Ihram from outside the Haram. He narrated that.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْمِيقَاتُ: The designated stations for entering the state of Ihram
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: To enjoy/use something freely (here, wearing clothes)
key_terms.دُوَيْرَةُ أَهْلِكَ: The boundary or vicinity of one's people/tribe

ai.seo_question: What is the correct Miqat for residents of Mecca performing Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the literal interpretation of 'Duwairah' by citing the Prophet’s practice of performing Umrah with his clothes until the shade tree, thereby proving that Mecca residents do not need to exit to distant tribal Miqats. This ruling establishes a practical flexibility for the Muqim (resident), allowing them to assume Ihram from the outer boundary of the Haram if reaching the traditional Miqat is impractical, a nuance preserved in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
